title: the monitor switch in Qwen3-0.6B does not ride on the attention sink's three slowest RoPE pairs
head: Training reused the attention sink’s head, but wrote the behave-when-watched switch into other parts of its keys
q: Does the monitor switch write into the attention sink’s 3 slowest RoPE pairs?
sub: Copying only those 3 of 64 pairs from the unwatched run moved {band0} and {band1} of the switch; the other 61 pairs moved {comp0} and {comp1} (2 training runs, 200 test prompts).
note: Reward taught the model to flatter less while a probe reads it. The probe is not in the text: it changes the model’s numbers a little, and the switch reads that change at the 3 yellow tokens.
kv_text: RoPE turns each pair at its own speed. The 3 slowest (pink) hold the attention sink: removing them takes away {sinkcut} of the attention on the first token in the last 2 layers.
ex_head: Layer 27, head 8: the head behind the switch · shading = where it looks from the answer

rows.swap: Watched, but the not-watched keys copied in at the 3 yellow tokens:

strip_head: Share of the switch moved · all 200 test prompts · 100% = answers as when not watched
bottom: No. Removing the 3 slowest pairs takes away {sinkcut} of the sink, but copying them moves only {band0} and {band1} of the switch. The other 61 pairs move {comp0} and {comp1}.
foot: Qwen3-0.6B, 2 reward-trained copies, last 2 layers trained · 200 test prompts · Nov 2026 · blog.kran.ai/lab
